briefdescription.para: Determine if its more efficient to fold: reduce(trunc(x)) -> trunc(reduce(x)).

This method looks for groups of shuffles acting on binops, of the form: x = shuffle ... y = shuffle ... a = binop x, y b = binop x, y shuffle a, b, selectmask We may, especially if the shuffle is wider than legal, be able to convert the shuffle to a form where only parts of a and b need to be computed.

detaileddescription.para: On architectures with no obvious "select" shuffle, this can reduce the total number of operations if the target reports them as cheaper.

briefdescription.para: Check if instruction depends on ZExt and this ZExt can be moved after the instruction.

detaileddescription.para: Move ZExt if it is profitable. For example: logic(zext(x),y) -> zext(logic(x,trunc(y))) lshr((zext(x),y) -> zext(lshr(x,trunc(y))) Cost model calculations takes into account if zext(x) has other users and whether it can be propagated through them too.
